memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "This is the law that applies when a person dies in a tent: Anyone who enters the tent and anyone who is in it will be unclean for seven days, and every open container without a lid fastened on it will be unclean. Anyone out in the open who touches someone who has been killed with a sword or someone who dies a natural death, or anyone who touches a human bone or a grave, will be unclean for seven days." — Num 19:14-16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
These verses show how far ceremonial uncleanness could spread. Enter a tent where death had occurred, and you became unclean. Even open containers within became defiled. Touch a bone or a grave in the open field, and uncleanness clung to you. Defilement spread easily and reached widely, touching people and objects alike.

There is a spiritual picture here worth pausing over. Defilement spreads; purity does not spread the same way. One unclean thing could make many things unclean, but cleanness was not so easily transferred. It reflects a sobering reality about sin: its corruption moves quickly, touching more than we intend, spreading further than we imagine.

We see this in life. A single harsh word can sour a whole household. One compromise can pull others down. Sin rarely stays contained; it reaches out and affects those around us. The people of Israel were being taught to take defilement seriously, because its influence was not easily controlled.

But the gospel brings astonishing news that reverses this pattern. In Jesus, purity became the thing that spreads. When He touched lepers, He was not defiled; they were healed. When He met the unclean, His holiness overcame their uncleanness rather than being overcome by it. In Christ, the flow is reversed: His cleansing power reaches out and makes the unclean clean. Where sin once spread its corruption, the grace of Christ now spreads its healing. Joined to Him, we carry not defilement but the life-giving purity He gives.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you seen how easily sin's influence spreads to others?
2. Why is it significant that Jesus' purity overcame uncleanness rather than being overcome?
3. How can you carry the cleansing influence of Christ to those around you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me to take seriously how easily sin spreads and affects those around me. Thank You that in Christ, purity now overcomes defilement. Let me carry His cleansing grace and healing influence into the lives I touch. Amen.
